summary: Prefill through host-resident routed experts: chunk size from the grouped projection's measured rate curve, layer double-buffered expert copies, and the FP64 reference any grouped projection is checked against
implementation_scope: Python schedule: rate-curve knee, chunk choice, expected touched experts, whole-layer copy decision, double-buffered step timeline, prefill estimate and staging size; Python FP64 reference of the routed SwiGLU block (stable route order, BF16/FP8 row/NVFP4/MXFP4 decoders, moe_block). The grouped projection is a provider's (kernels.json); the router, copies, events, attention and dense layers are the engine's.

agent_guidance.use_when: Prefill of an expert-routed model whose routed experts live mostly in host memory, so a prompt chunk's time is dominated by copying non-resident experts and the prefill rate grows with the chunk size
agent_guidance.avoid_when: Every expert fits on the device (measure a provider's grouped GEMM for the format first), or decode steps that route a few tokens (device-expert-cache and GEMV-shaped rows instead)
provides: Chunk choice at the knee of the measured rate curve under the workspace bound, expected touched experts per layer and the whole-layer copy decision
A double-buffered step timeline and a prefill estimate with its copy-only floor, and staging buffer sizes
An FP64 reference of the routed SwiGLU block (stable route order, the formats' decoders, moe_block) to check any grouped projection against on the target
kernels.json: the provider grouped projections with their calls, formats, GPUs and shapes
engine_supplies: Router ids and weights per chunk, the attention and dense layers and the residual add
The grouped projection from kernels.json (or its own), checked against moe_block on the target
The expert pointer table per step and the staging buffers, taken from memory decode leaves unused while a prompt runs
Copy-engine copies into the staging buffers with the events that order them against compute
Measured rates by rows per expert on the target, step times at the chosen chunk and non-resident bytes per layer
preserve: No reduction split by the row count and no atomics in a token's sum
A staging buffer refilled only after its last step has finished computing
Every routed expert of a step resident, staged or readable before the projection reads it
Measured points only: no interpolated rates or times
adapt: The projection: any kernel from kernels.json or the engine's own, measured against them, with SwiGLU and the combine fused or not
Chunk policy, knee fraction and the whole-layer copy threshold
A measured CPU share for rarely routed experts instead of copying them

code_files.purpose: Rate-curve knee, chunk choice, touched experts, whole-layer copies, double-buffered timeline, prefill estimate and staging size
FP64 reference of the routed SwiGLU block: decoders, stable route order, moe_block

requires.hardware: Python 3.11+ standard library; the grouped projection's GPU as kernels.json lists
requires.model: Expert-routed layers with top-k routing, gate/up/down experts and SwiGLU; projection output widths a multiple of 64 and input widths a multiple of 32
requires.workload: Prompts long enough for chunks to touch most experts of a layer, with routed experts mostly off the device

contract.input: For the schedule, measured rates by rows per expert, step times, non-resident bytes and the link rate; for the reference, activations, routes, routing weights and each expert's stored matrices
contract.output: Chunk size, step timeline, prefill estimate and its copy-only floor; the reference's route order and FP64 block outputs
contract.ownership: Pure functions over the caller's values; the engine owns every buffer, stream and kernel
contract.failure: The schedule rejects empty or invalid curves, nonpositive rates and negative times or bytes; the reference rejects unknown formats
contract.core_boundary: No Core change; Core supplies allocations, streams and readiness

validation.host: Rate-curve knee, chunk choice and its workspace bound, touched experts, whole-layer copy decision, double-buffered timeline ordering, the estimate's copy-only floor, and the reference's decoders, route order and block on hand-computed cases
validation.native: None: the grouped projection is a provider's, checked against moe_block on the target
